questions.q: In sweet, one-third is sugar. If the price of sugar now is $\frac{7}{6}$ of the previous price, what is the effective percentage increase in the cost of the sweet?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, sweet me $\frac{1}{3}$ hissa sugar hai. Change sirf isi hisse me ho raha hai. Fraction ka direct multiply maar de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Sugar ka price $7/6$ ho gaya matlab increase $1/6$ ka hai. Sweet me sugar ki hissedari $1/3$ hai. Effective net increase $= 1/3 \times 1/6 = 1/18$. Percentage me nikalne ke liye $\times 100$ kar $\implies 100/18 = 50/9 = 100/18\%$ directly options me given hai.

Mathematically :-
$\text{Inc}_s = \frac{7}{6} - 1 = \frac{1}{6}$
$\text{Net Inc} = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{18}$
$\% = \frac{1}{18} \times 100 = \frac{100}{18}\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan le total sweet 300g hai. Sugar 100g, non-sugar 200g. Price assume kar. Calculation lamba jayega. Weighted average hi ultimate hai.

Mathematically :-
$\text{Let total} = 300g$
$\text{Sugar} = 100g, \text{Other} = 200g$
$\text{Old Cost} = 100(6) + 200(C)$
$\text{New Cost} = 100(7) + 200(C)$
$\text{Diff} = 100$
$\% = \frac{100}{1800} = \frac{100}{18}\%$

Exam Takeaway: Partial changes nikalne ke liye hamesha (Fraction of weight) $\times$ (Fraction of change) use karo.

questions.q: Volume of a sphere is increased by 119.7% when its radius is increased then find % change in TSA of sphere?
questions.s:

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): 3D volume se 1D radius, aur fir 2D surface area par aao.

Mathematically :-
$$V_{ratio} = 1000 : 2197 \\\\ R_{ratio} = \sqrt[3]{1000} : \sqrt[3]{2197} = 10 : 13 \\\\ TSA_{ratio} = 10^2 : 13^2 = 100 : 169 \\\\ Change = (169 - 100) = 69\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Volume ki equation aur powers ko manually shift karo.

Mathematically :-
$$\frac{V_2}{V_1} = 2.197 = (\frac{R_2}{R_1})^3 \\\\ \frac{R_2}{R_1} = 1.3 \\\\ \frac{TSA_2}{TSA_1} = (1.3)^2 = 1.69 \\\\ \% \ Change = (1.69 - 1) \times 100 = 69\%$$

Exam Takeaway: $1$ se $20$ tak cubes yaad hone chahiye. 3D se 1D aana ho toh cube root, aur fir 2D ke liye square.

questions.q: The population of a village 4 years ago was 3,20,000. Due to migration to cities, it decreases at the rate of 5% every year. Find the decrease in its population in the last 4 years.
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, $5\%$ decrease ko 4 baar multiply karna mout hai. Digital Sum (DS) laga! 320000 ka DS 5 hai. Multiplier $0.95$ ka DS 5 hai. Toh New Pop ka DS = $5 \times 5^4 = 5^5$. $5^2 = 25 \implies 7$. $5^5 = 25 \times 25 \times 5 \implies 7 \times 7 \times 5 = 49 \times 5 \implies 4 \times 5 = 20 \implies 2$. Drop = $5 - 2 = 3$. Options me DS 3 sirf ek ka hai: 59358.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Digital Sum completely replaces calculation.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Old Pop DS} = 3+2+0 = 5 \\ \text{Factor DS} = 1 - 0.05 = 0.95 \implies 14 \implies 5 \\ \text{New Pop DS} = 5 \times (5)^4 = 5 \times 625 \implies 5 \times 13 \implies 5 \times 4 = 20 \implies 2 \\ \text{Decrease DS} = 5 - 2 = 3 \\ \text{Check Opt 2:} 5+9+3+5+8 = 30 \implies 3 \text{ (Match!)} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Fractional multipliers approach.

Mathematically :-
$$ A = P \left(1 - \frac{r}{100}\right)^t \\ A = 320000 \times \left(\frac{19}{20}\right)^4 \\ A = 320000 \times \frac{130321}{160000} \\ A = 2 \times 130321 = 260642 \\ \text{Decrease} = 320000 - 260642 = 59358 $$

Exam Takeaway: Power 3 ya 4 aaye aur end values messy hon toh DS sabse pehla weapon hona chahiye.

questions.q: A farmer allocates his entire fixed farm land to grow only two fodder crops: Bajra and Jowar. In the last season, the land allocated to Bajra was 14.28\% less than the land allocated to Jowar. This season, he increases the land for Jowar by 28.56\%. If the total cultivated farm area remains exactly the same and the new area for Bajra becomes 120 acres, what is the total area of the farm?
questions.s: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation: $A + B = K$ (Total farm land is constant. Fodder area gain in one crop = Exact absolute area loss in the other). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Kheti-baari aur chaare (fodder) ka simple logic laga. Total zameen toh fix hai na? Agar ek fasal ka area badhega, toh doosri ka utna hi kam hona padega. Percentages dekh kar darna nahi hai: $14.28\%$ dekhte hi dimaag mein $1/7$ aana chahiye aur $28.56\%$ dekhte hi $2/7$ aana chahiye. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Ratio likh aur secondon mein uda de: $14.28\% = \frac{1}{7}$. Matlab base Jowar ($J$) ka $7$ unit maan le. Bajra ($B$) $1/7$ kam hai $\Rightarrow B = 7 - 1 = 6$ units. Total Area ($K$) = $B + J = 6 + 7 = 13 units. (Matlab answer 13 ka multiple hoga, options dekh ke hi 390 mark kar sakta tha!) Lekin cross-verify kar lete hain: Ab question kehta hai Jowar $28.56\%$ (yani $\frac{2}{7}$) badha. Jowar ka area $7$ units tha, usme $\frac{2}{7}$ badha = $+2$ units. Kyuki total zameen utni hi hai ($A+B=K$), Jowar ne jo $2$ unit zameen li, wo Bajra ke hisse se aayi hogi! Toh Bajra exactly $-2$ units kam hoga. Naya Bajra = $6 - 2 = 4$ units. Question mein naya Bajra $120$ acres diya hai. $\Rightarrow 4 \text{ units} = 120 \text{ acres}$ $\Rightarrow 1 \text{ unit} = 30 \text{ acres}$ Total Area = $13 \text{ units} = 13 \times 30 = 390 \text{ acres}$. Boom! Khatam. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let Total Area = $K$. $B + J = K$. Initial setup: $B = J - 0.1428 J = \frac{6}{7} J$. $\Rightarrow \frac{B}{J} = \frac{6}{7}$. Let $B = 6x$, $J = 7x$. Total $K = 13x$. New $J = 7x + (\frac{2}{7} \times 7x) = 9x$. Since Total $K = 13x$ is constant: New $B = K - \text{New } J = 13x - 9x = 4x$. Given $4x = 120 \Rightarrow x = 30$. Total area = $13x = 13(30) = 390$. Future Exam Takeaway: $A+B=K$ ka rule sirf elections ya expenditure mein nahi lagta. Land, Mixture, ya Investment—jahan bhi "Total" constant ho aur ek component badhe, toh direct doosre ko same absolute ratio unit se gira do! Koi $x$ nahi manna.

questions.q: If a student multiplied a number by $\frac{6}{11}$ instead of $\frac{5}{6}$ find the % error in the calculation?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Jab bhi fractions aapas me takraye, fractions ke denominators ka LCM number maan liya kar taaki decimal ka kachra na ho. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): 11 aur 6 ka LCM 66 hota hai. Maan le original number 66 hai. Sahi result aana tha: $66 \times \frac{5}{6} = 55$. Galati se result kya aaya: $66 \times \frac{6}{11} = 36$. Error kitne ka hua? $55 - 36 = 19$. Error humesha asli value (55) pe niklega. % Error = $\frac{19}{55} \times 100$. Ab isko thoda estimate kar: $55$ ka $10\% = 5.5$, toh $30\% = 16.5$. Us se upar hai, toh approx $34.5\%$ ke aspaas aayega. Exact fraction hoga $34 \frac{6}{11}\%$. Options dekhte hi idea lag jayega. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Cross multiply bhi use kar sakta hai. True value : Error value $= \frac{5}{6} : \frac{6}{11}$. Cross mar: $55 : 36$. Error 19 ka on 55. Wahi baat hai, bas representation alag. questions.q: The income of Manju is Rs. 6000 and his income is increased by 25%, then decreased by x% and there after increased by (x – 10)%. Find the income of Manju after a rise of (x – 10)%, If the income of Manju after a decrease of x% is the same as his initial salary.

Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, steps me tod isko. 6k ka 25% jyada 7.5k hua. Wapas 6k aana hai toh kitna kam hua? 1.5k. 1.5k 7.5k ka kitna hai? Seedha $20\%$. Matlab $x=20$ nikal aya.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Value shift fraction se x nikal aur final me add karde.

Mathematically :-
$$6000 \times 1.25 = 7500 \\\\ Decrease = \frac{7500 - 6000}{7500} = \frac{1500}{7500} = \frac{1}{5} = 20\% \Rightarrow x = 20 \\\\ Final \ Rise = (20 - 10)\% = 10\% \\\\ Final \ Income = 6000 \times 1.10 = 6600$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Base equation banakar equation solve karo.

Mathematically :-
$$6000(1 + \frac{25}{100})(1 - \frac{x}{100}) = 6000 \\\\ 1.25 (1 - \frac{x}{100}) = 1 \\\\ 1 - \frac{x}{100} = \frac{4}{5} \Rightarrow x = 20 \\\\ New = 6000(1 + \frac{10}{100}) = 6600$$

Exam Takeaway: Language ko portions me decode karo, x ki value direct base shift karne se aati hai.

questions.q: A student gets 66 marks more in French than what she got in German. Her German marks are $28\%$ of the sum of her French and German marks. What are her French marks?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product Method (Ratio Conversion)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $28\% = \frac{7}{25}$ hota hai. Toh German ke marks $7$ unit hue out of $25$. Bacha French jiske marks $18$ unit honge. Answer hamesha $18$ ka multiple hoga. Direct $108$ chamak raha hai na?

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Seedha percentage ko fraction me phek kar maar! Mathematically :- $$ 28\% = \frac{7}{25} \\ G = 7, F = 25 - 7 = 18 \implies F:G = 18:7 \\ F - G = 11 \text{ units} = 66 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 6 \\ F = 18 \times 6 = 108 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Equations solve karne me bahut waqt niklega. Mathematically :- $$ G = 0.28(F + G) \\ G = 0.28F + 0.28G \implies 0.72G = 0.28F \\ \frac{F}{G} = \frac{72}{28} = \frac{18}{7} \\ F - G = 66 \implies 18x - 7x = 66 \implies 11x = 66 \implies x = 6 \\ F = 18(6) = 108 $$

Exam Takeaway: Sum relation aate hi fractional base $100$ ko directly ratio logic me tod do taaki difference asani se compare ho jaye.

questions.q: The strength of SSC Aspirants increases and decreases every alternate year. It starts with increase by 20% and thereafter the percentage of increase/decrease is the same. Which of the following is definitely true about the strength of SSC Aspirants in 2000 as compared to that in 1996?
questions.s:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, 4 saal ka chain reaction hai: +20\%, -20\%, +20\%, -20\%. Jab bhi same percentage badhe aur ghate, humesha net decrease hi hota hai. Seedha loss ka formula dimag me chamakna chahiye.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Base 100 maan. 4 baar successive chalega: $100 \times 1.2 \times 0.8 \times 1.2 \times 0.8 = 100 \times 0.96 \times 0.96$. 96 ka square nikalna bahut aasan hai (100 se 4 kam hai, toh $96-4=92$ aur $4^2=16$), yani 0.9216. Final value hui 92.16. 100 se ghat kar 92.16 aane me seedha 7.84\% ka decrease!

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Successive ko pairs me tod. +20\% aur -20\% ka ek pair net change $\frac{-20^2}{100} = -4\%$ deta hai. Aise 2 pair hain, yani do baar -4\% ka successive. Net change = $-4 - 4 + \frac{(-4)(-4)}{100} = -8 + 0.16 = -7.84\%$.

**Exam Takeaway:** Successive calculation ko fractions ya pairs me todne se answer hawa me nikalta hai. $x$ badhe aur $x$ ghate $\implies$ Humesha $\frac{x^2}{100}$ ka loss.

questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Kharcha same hai. Pehle jo value $33 \%$ thi wahi ab $27 \%$ ho gayi naye income par. Fraction ratio le aur kissa khatam kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Amount constant hone par percentage aur base inversely proportional hote hain.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Ratio of Percentages} = 33 \% : 27 \% = 11 : 9 \\ \text{Ratio of Incomes} = 9 : 11 \\ \text{Increase in units} = 2 \text{ units} \\ 2 \text{ units} = 1000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 500 \\ \text{Initial Income (9 units)} = 9 \times 500 = 4500 $$

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial Income} = I \\ 33 \% \text{ of } I = 27 \% \text{ of } (I + 1000) \\ 33I = 27I + 27000 \\ 6I = 27000 \\ I = 4500 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab expenditure ya koi bhi value constant hoti hai, toh unke base (Income) ka ratio seedha unke percentage ratio ka ulta hota hai.

questions.q: The price of an article increased by $16.66\%$ every year. If the difference between the price at the end of third and fourth year is 126 then 1/8th of the price at the end of second year?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $16.66\%$ badhne ka fraction 1/6 hota hai. Koi chiz 3rd year se 4th year me jayegi, toh kitna badhegi? Apne aap ka 1/6 hi badhegi na! Yahi trick thi isme.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): 4th year aur 3rd year ka difference, purely 3rd year ki value ka $1/6$ hai. Toh $3\text{rd yr} \times 1/6 = 126 \implies 3\text{rd yr} = 756$. Ab isse backward ja 2nd year pe (multiply by 6/7). $756 \times 6/7 = 648$. Iska $1/8$ nikal, $648 / 8 = 81$. Ratio method is supreme!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Diff} = P_3 \times \frac{1}{6} = 126$
$P_3 = 756$
$P_2 = 756 \times \frac{6}{7} = 648$
$\text{Ans} = \frac{648}{8} = 81$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $P \times (7/6)^3$ aur $P \times (7/6)^4$ leke dono ko minus karke P ki value nikalne jayega toh adha exam wahi khatam ho jayega.

Mathematically :-
$P(1+\frac{1}{6})^4 - P(1+\frac{1}{6})^3 = 126$
$P(\frac{7}{6})^3 (\frac{7}{6} - 1) = 126$
$P_3 \times \frac{1}{6} = 126 \implies P_3 = 756$
$P_2 \times \frac{7}{6} = 756 \implies P_2 = 648$
$\frac{P_2}{8} = 81$

Exam Takeaway: Compound growth me adjacent years ka difference direct fraction increase ki value bata deta hai.

questions.q: In a state election between two parties, $83\%$ of the voters cast their votes, out of which $4\%$ of the votes were declared invalid. Party A got 156611 votes which were $83\%$ of the total valid votes. Find the total number of votes enrolled in that election. (Consider integer part only)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, options bohot dhyan se dekh. Ek option out of bounds hai (23 lakh) aur baaki teen me accha khasa gap hai. Question me (Consider integer part only) likha hai, iska clear ishara hai ki calculation exact cut nahi hogi aur decimals aayenge. Yahan tera Digital Sum ya Unit Digit completely fail ho jayega. Approximation hi ekmatra bachaav hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Nearest fraction approximation se hack kar. $83\%$ ko thoda bada maanke $83.33\%$ (yani $\frac{5}{6}$) assume kar le, aur $96\%$ ko direct $\frac{24}{25}$ likh. Humne equation me value thodi badi mani hai, toh hamara jo approximate result aayega, actual answer usse thoda sa bada hona chahiye.

Mathematically :-
$$Total \times \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{24}{25} \times \frac{5}{6} \approx 156611 \\ Total \times \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{5}{6} \approx 156611 \\ Total \times \frac{2}{3} \approx 156611 \\ Total \approx 156611 \times \frac{3}{2} \\ Total \approx 234916.5$$

Kyuki humne base bada mana tha, answer thoda bada hoga. Option D (2,34,888) chhota ho gaya, agla seedha 2,36,807 hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Base Scaling Shift. Agar fractions yaad na aayein, toh direct decimal se hi first 2 digits ko estimate kar lo aur aage ki calculation avoid karo. Ye method calculation speed demand karega.

Mathematically :-
$$Total \times 0.83 \times 0.96 \times 0.83 = 156611 \\ Total \times (0.83)^2 \times 0.96 = 156611 \\ Total \times 0.6889 \times 0.96 = 156611 \\ Total \times 0.661344 = 156611 \\ Total = \frac{156611}{0.661344} \approx 236807$$

Exam Takeaway: TCS aise sawal exam me time khane aur pressure banane ke liye deta hai. Fractions ki approximate hack maar ke option choose kar, exact division me ghusega toh do aur aasan sawalo ka time chala jayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

questions.q: At the beginning of day 1 of a month, Rajesh has 500 eggs. He sells 20% of the eggs by the end of the day and added b% of the eggs at the beginning of the next day and sold 20% of the eggs at the end of the next day. This pattern continued up to the end of the third day of the month when he is left with 1024 eggs. The value of b is equal to:
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, sequence break kar. Day 1 ke end me 500 ka $80\%$ bacha (yani 400). Fir 2 din same multiplier laga. 400 se badhkar 1024 pahuchna hai. Perfect square banega. Option se utha, agar $b=100$ (yani double), toh $400 \times 2 = 800$, usme se $20\%$ gaye bache 640. Phir agle din $640 \times 2 = 1280$, $20\%$ gaye bache 1024. Match ho gaya!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Hit and Trial sequence.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{End of Day 1} = 500 \times 0.8 = 400 \\ \text{Check } b=100 \implies \text{add } 100\% \implies \text{multiply by } 2 \\ \text{End of Day 2} = (400 \times 2) \times 0.8 = 800 \times 0.8 = 640 \\ \text{End of Day 3} = (640 \times 2) \times 0.8 = 1280 \times 0.8 = 1024 \text{ (Matched!)} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Full equation with successive multipliers.

Mathematically :-
$$ 400 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 \times (0.8)^2 = 1024 \\ 400 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 \times 0.64 = 1024 \\ 256 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 = 1024 \\ \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 = \frac{1024}{256} = 4 \\ 1 + \frac{b}{100} = 2 \implies \frac{b}{100} = 1 \implies b = 100 $$

Exam Takeaway: Complex equation me hamesha perfect square pattern dhundha kar aur option satisfy karaya kar.

questions.q: The ratio of the monthly income of P to the monthly income of Q is 7:10, and P's saving is $21\frac{3}{7}\%$ more than Q's savings. Find the expenditure of P if the sum of the monthly income of P and Q is $85,000$, and the expenditure of Q is $22,000$.
questions.s:
[Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling]

Pen-Free Observation: $7+10 = 17$ units $= 85000$. $1 \text{ unit} = 5000$. P ki income $35k$, Q ki $50k$. Q ki saving = Income - Exp = $50k - 22k = 28k$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Income $P = 35,000$, $Q = 50,000$.
Q ki saving $= 50,000 - 22,000 = 28,000$.
P ki saving Q se $21\frac{3}{7}\%$ zyada hai. Percentage ka fraction bana: $21\frac{3}{7}\% = \frac{150}{7}\% = \frac{150}{700} = \frac{3}{14}$.
P's saving $= 28,000 + (28,000 \times \frac{3}{14}) = 28,000 + 6,000 = 34,000$.
P ka exp $= \text{Income} - \text{Saving} = 35,000 - 34,000 = 1,000$.

Takeaway: Weird percentages ko hamesha fraction me tod lo, exam setter wahi values deta hai jo denominator se cut jayen (jaise $28000$ aur $14$).

questions.q: The total count of premium and standard seats in a theater remains constant over two months. On Monday, premium seats were in the majority by '$x$'. If the standard seats strictly increased by $40\%$, and the total capacity of the theater is $5500$, find the original number of premium seats.

Core Conceptual Tool: JSM (Constant Sum Shifting)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab sum constant hota hai (Total seats 5500 fix hain), toh ek variable jitna badhega, doosra utna hi ghatega. Gap of difference ka aadha entity ka absolute shift hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Gap in majority ko find kar aur percentage given ke hisab se shift ko resolve kar le. Seedhi baat.

Mathematically :-
$$ Gap = x - (-3x) = 4x \\\\ \\Delta S = \\frac{4x}{2} = 2x \\\\ 40\\% \\ of \\ S_{init} = 2x \\implies S_{init} = 5x \\\\ P_{init} = 5x + x = 6x \\\\ Total = 11x = 5500 \\implies x = 500 \\\\ P_{init} = 6(500) = 3000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebra lagakar shift equations me substitution kar.

Mathematically :-
$$ P - S = x \\\\ S_{new} - P_{new} = 3x \\\\ S_{new} = 1.4S \\\\ P + S = 5500 \\\\ (1.4S - 3x) + 1.4S = 5500 \\\\ 2.8S - 3x = 5500 \\\\ (S+x) + S = 5500 \\implies 2S = 5500 - x \\\\ x = 500 \\implies P = 3000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Election waale sum-constant models ko kisi bhi $A+B=K$ scenario mein chipkaya jaa sakta hai. 'Difference of differences divided by 2' wala hack hamesha lagta hai jab interchanging shifts ho!

questions_hin.s_hi:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, $5\%$ decrease ko 4 baar multiply karna mout hai. Digital Sum (DS) laga! 320000 ka DS 5 hai. Multiplier $0.95$ ka DS 5 hai. Toh New Pop ka DS = $5 \times 5^4 = 5^5$. $5^2 = 25 \implies 7$. $5^5 = 25 \times 25 \times 5 \implies 7 \times 7 \times 5 = 49 \times 5 \implies 4 \times 5 = 20 \implies 2$. Drop = $5 - 2 = 3$. Options me DS 3 sirf ek ka hai: 59358.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Digital Sum completely replaces calculation.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Old Pop DS} = 3+2+0 = 5 \\ \text{Factor DS} = 1 - 0.05 = 0.95 \implies 14 \implies 5 \\ \text{New Pop DS} = 5 \times (5)^4 = 5 \times 625 \implies 5 \times 13 \implies 5 \times 4 = 20 \implies 2 \\ \text{Decrease DS} = 5 - 2 = 3 \\ \text{Check Opt 2:} 5+9+3+5+8 = 30 \implies 3 \text{ (Match!)} $$

Fractional multipliers approach.

Mathematically :-

questions_hin.q_hi: A farmer allocates his entire fixed farm land to grow only two fodder crops: Bajra and Jowar. In the last season, the land allocated to Bajra was 14.28\% less than the land allocated to Jowar. This season, he increases the land for Jowar by 28.56\%. If the total cultivated farm area remains exactly the same and the new area for Bajra becomes 120 acres, what is the total area of the farm?
questions_hin.s_hi: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation: $A + B = K$ (Total farm land is constant. Fodder area gain in one crop = Exact absolute area loss in the other). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Kheti-baari aur chaare (fodder) ka simple logic laga. Total zameen toh fix hai na? Agar ek fasal ka area badhega, toh doosri ka utna hi kam hona padega. Percentages dekh kar darna nahi hai: $14.28\%$ dekhte hi dimaag mein $1/7$ aana chahiye aur $28.56\%$ dekhte hi $2/7$ aana chahiye. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Ratio likh aur secondon mein uda de: $14.28\% = \frac{1}{7}$. Matlab base Jowar ($J$) ka $7$ unit maan le. Bajra ($B$) $1/7$ kam hai $\Rightarrow B = 7 - 1 = 6$ units. Total Area ($K$) = $B + J = 6 + 7 = 13 units. (Matlab answer 13 ka multiple hoga, options dekh ke hi 390 mark kar sakta tha!) Lekin cross-verify kar lete hain: Ab question kehta hai Jowar $28.56\%$ (yani $\frac{2}{7}$) badha. Jowar ka area $7$ units tha, usme $\frac{2}{7}$ badha = $+2$ units. Kyuki total zameen utni hi hai ($A+B=K$), Jowar ne jo $2$ unit zameen li, wo Bajra ke hisse se aayi hogi! Toh Bajra exactly $-2$ units kam hoga. Naya Bajra = $6 - 2 = 4$ units. Question mein naya Bajra $120$ acres diya hai. $\Rightarrow 4 \text{ units} = 120 \text{ acres}$ $\Rightarrow 1 \text{ unit} = 30 \text{ acres}$ Total Area = $13 \text{ units} = 13 \times 30 = 390 \text{ acres}$. Boom! Khatam. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let Total Area = $K$. $B + J = K$. Initial setup: $B = J - 0.1428 J = \frac{6}{7} J$. $\Rightarrow \frac{B}{J} = \frac{6}{7}$. Let $B = 6x$, $J = 7x$. Total $K = 13x$. New $J = 7x + (\frac{2}{7} \times 7x) = 9x$. Since Total $K = 13x$ is constant: New $B = K - \text{New } J = 13x - 9x = 4x$. Given $4x = 120 \Rightarrow x = 30$. Total area = $13x = 13(30) = 390$. Future Exam Takeaway: $A+B=K$ ka rule sirf elections ya expenditure mein nahi lagta. Land, Mixture, ya Investment—jahan bhi "Total" constant ho aur ek component badhe, toh direct doosre ko same absolute ratio unit se gira do! Koi $x$ nahi manna.

questions_hin.q_hi: A student gets 66 marks more in French than what she got in German. Her German marks are $28\%$ of the sum of her French and German marks. What are her French marks?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product Method (Ratio Conversion)

questions_hin.q_hi: At the beginning of day 1 of a month, Rajesh has 500 eggs. He sells 20% of the eggs by the end of the day and added b% of the eggs at the beginning of the next day and sold 20% of the eggs at the end of the next day. This pattern continued up to the end of the third day of the month when he is left with 1024 eggs. The value of b is equal to:
questions_hin.s_hi:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, sequence break kar. Day 1 ke end me 500 ka $80\%$ bacha (yani 400). Fir 2 din same multiplier laga. 400 se badhkar 1024 pahuchna hai. Perfect square banega. Option se utha, agar $b=100$ (yani double), toh $400 \times 2 = 800$, usme se $20\%$ gaye bache 640. Phir agle din $640 \times 2 = 1280$, $20\%$ gaye bache 1024. Match ho gaya!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Hit and Trial sequence.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{End of Day 1} = 500 \times 0.8 = 400 \\ \text{Check } b=100 \implies \text{add } 100\% \implies \text{multiply by } 2 \\ \text{End of Day 2} = (400 \times 2) \times 0.8 = 800 \times 0.8 = 640 \\ \text{End of Day 3} = (640 \times 2) \times 0.8 = 1280 \times 0.8 = 1024 \text{ (Matched!)} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Full equation with successive multipliers.

Mathematically :-
$$ 400 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 \times (0.8)^2 = 1024 \\ 400 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 \times 0.64 = 1024 \\ 256 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 = 1024 \\ \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 = \frac{1024}{256} = 4 \\ 1 + \frac{b}{100} = 2 \implies \frac{b}{100} = 1 \implies b = 100 $$

Exam Takeaway: Complex equation me hamesha perfect square pattern dhundha kar aur option satisfy karaya kar.

Income $P = 35,000$, $Q = 50,000$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Gap in majority ko find kar aur percentage given ke hisab se shift ko resolve kar le. Seedhi baat.

$$ Gap = x - (-3x) = 4x \\\\ \\Delta S = \\frac{4x}{2} = 2x \\\\ 40\\% \\ of \\ S_{init} = 2x \\implies S_{init} = 5x \\\\ P_{init} = 5x + x = 6x \\\\ Total = 11x = 5500 \\implies x = 500 \\\\ P_{init} = 6(500) = 3000 $$

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, seedha Third number ko 100 maan.
Toh First hua $= 70$. Second hua $= 63$.
Pucha kya hai? Second first se kitna chota hai?
Difference $= 70 - 63 = 7$.
Percentage on First $= \frac{7}{70} \times 100 = 10\%$.
Options me 7% janbujh kar rakha gaya hai taki bache fatafat $37-30=7$ mark karein aur gadhe kehlayein.
